messages:
carol: CI image push failing on canary after my Dockerfile stage reorder. build job shows a tar layer decompress error and registry returned 422. job: https://ci.redwood.internal/5678

raj: can you paste the last few log lines? and was this the PR that touched the multistage order?

carol: yep PR #842 changed the order to combine assets earlier. logs:```
# buildkit: extracting layer 7/12
error: zstd decompression: checksum mismatch
failed to upload blob: unexpected status code 422 Unprocessable Entity - "invalid layer payload"
```

mina: hmmm checksum mismatch implies a corrupted tar stream or cache returned bad blob. did buildx use a cache import?

carol: buildx used the default cache from our registry. I also see a few `unexpected EOF` earlier. I triggered a rerun already (ci-bot rerun).

devops-bot: token-rotation event at 2026-03-17T12:05:10Z for registry-auth-service. Affected services: registry-cache-proxy.

raj: token rotation could cause interrupted uploads -> half-uploaded layers in cache. quick triage: 1) try a fresh build with `--no-cache` 2) prune cache entries for that repo 3) if repro, bisect the dockerfile reorder commit.

carol: running local reproduce now: `DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 --no-cache --progress=plain .`

alex: also try forcing `--push` to a temp registry `staging-registry.redwood.svc` to see if origin registry is the culprit. if temp push works, we know the origin has corrupted cache blobs.

mina: commands that helped last time:```sh
# remove specific cache from buildx
docker buildx du --verbose
docker buildx prune --filter type=local --all --force
# remove remote cache reference (if using registry cache import)
docker buildx build --cache-to=type=registry,ref=staging-registry.redwood.svc/cache/tmp --cache-from=type=registry,ref=staging-registry.redwood.svc/cache/tmp --no-cache
```

carol: re-run with --no-cache + pushing to staging-registry now. if that succeeds i'll then run a prune on the main registry cache.

raj: if prune required on production registry, coordinate with infra to avoid impacting other pipelines. ping @infra-weekend if low-traffic window not available.

devops-bot: noted. scheduled maintenance window suggestion posted: https://infra.redwood.internal/maintenance/2026-03-18

carol: update: local no-cache build succeeded and pushed to staging-registry fine. so root registry likely had corrupted cache entries. I'm going to open a support ticket with registry team and schedule a cache prune for the low-traffic window.

alex: thanks. for the immediate hotfix we can revert the multistage reorder if needed, but since staging push passed, i think prune + re-run CI is fine. can you paste the CI job id here when you trigger the prune-run?

carol: will do. CI job id for the failing run: 2026-03-17-5678. i'll update this thread after infra prune. :thumbsup:

mina: FYI, let's add a small check in our CI that rejects manifest finalization errors like `invalid layer payload` and retries the push with `--no-cache` automatically once, to reduce manual triage for flaky registry artifacts.

raj: agreed. can be a short step in the build pipeline. filing a tiny ticket after we close the prune task.

carol: filing infra ticket now and scheduling prune for 2026-03-18 02:00 UTC. will follow up here after it's done.

devops-bot: ticket created: REG-3124 (registry cache prune request)

carol: closing loop: infra pruned cache, CI rerun passed. marking as resolved. thanks folks! :party_popper:
